16	
17	# LaTeX 论文写作全流程
18	
19	ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
31	| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
95	5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
96	```
97	
98	### 3.3 API 速查
99	
100	| API | 用途 | 限制 |
101	|-----|------|------|
102	| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
103	| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
104	| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |
105	
106	```python
107	# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
108	import requests
109	def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
110	    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
111	                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
112	    r.raise_for_status()
113	    return r.text
114	
115	# Semantic Scholar 搜索
116	from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
117	sch = SemanticScholar()
118	results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
119	for p in results:
120	    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
121	```
122	
123	### 3.4 引用处理规则
124	
125	| 情况 | 处理 |
126	|------|------|
127	| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
128	| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
129	| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
130	| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
131	| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 4. 顶会模板速查
136	
137	### 4.1 ML/AI 会议
138	
139	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
140	|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
141	| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
142	| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
143	| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
144	| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
145	| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
146	| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |
147	
148	### 4.2 系统会议
149	
150	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
151	|------|---------|---------|---------|
152	| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
153	| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
154	| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
155	| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |
156	
157	### 4.3 模板使用原则
158	
159	```bash
160	# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
161	cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/
162	
163	# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
164	latexmk -pdf main.tex
165	
166	# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
167	```
168	
169	**禁止事项：**
170	- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
171	- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
172	- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. 写作规范
177	
178	### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）
179	
180	花**大致相等**的时间在：
181	1. Abstract
182	2. Introduction
183	3. 图表
184	4. **其余所有内容加起来**
185	
186	审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。
187	
188	### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）
189	
190	```
191	1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
192	2. 为什么这很难且重要
193	3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
194	4. 有什么证据
195	5. 最惊人的数字/结果
196	```
197	
198	删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~
199	
200	### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）
201	
202	| 原则 | 规则 |
203	|------|------|
204	| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
205	| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
206	| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
207	| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |
208	
209	### 5.4 常见修改
210	
211	| 问题 | 修复 |
212	|------|------|
213	| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
214	| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
215	| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
216	| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |
217	
218	---
219	
220	## 6. 投稿工程链
221	
222	### 6.1 构建
223	
224	```bash
225	# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
226	latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
227	
228	# 手动：需要多次编译
229	pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
230	```
231	
232	### 6.2 Lint + 格式化
233	
234	```bash
235	# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
236	chktex main.tex
237	
238	# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
239	latexindent -w main.tex
240	```
241	
242	### 6.3 图表格式
243	
244	| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
245	|------|------|------|
246	| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
247	| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
248	| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |
249	
250	```latex
251	\usepackage{booktabs}
252	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
253	\toprule
254	Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
255	\midrule
256	Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
257	\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
258	\bottomrule
259	\end{tabular}
260	```
261	
262	**图表规范：**
263	- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
264	- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
265	- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
266	- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）
267	
268	### 6.4 投稿打包
269	
270	```bash
271	# 清理辅助文件
272	latexmk -c
273	
274	# 打包投稿
275	zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
276	```
277	
278	### 6.5 常见失败点
279	
280	| 问题 | 解决 |
281	|------|------|
282	| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
283	| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
284	| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
285	| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
286	| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |
287	
288	---
289	
290	## 7. 会议转投
291	
292	当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：
293	
294	### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换
295	
296	| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
297	|------|---------|---------|
298	| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
299	| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
300	| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
301	| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |
302	
303	### 7.2 转投原则
304	
305	1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
306	2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
307	3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
308	4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 8. 投前清单
313	
314	### 通用清单
315	
316	- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
317	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
318	- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
319	- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
320	- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
321	- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
322	- [ ] 符合页数限制
323	- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
324	- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
325	- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning
326	
327	### 会议特定
328	
329	| 会议 | 额外要求 |
330	|------|---------|
331	| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
332	| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
333	| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
334	| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
335	| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |
336	
337	---
338	
339	## 参考资源
340	
341	**写作方法论：**
342	- [Neel Nanda: How to Write ML Papers](https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/eJGptPbbFPZGLpjsp/) — What/Why/So What 框架
343	- [Farquhar: How to Write ML Papers](https://sebastianfarquhar.com/on-research/2024/11/04/how_to_write_ml_papers/) — 五句法 Abstract
344	- [Gopen & Swan: Science of Scientific Writing](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~swanson/papers/science-of-writing.pdf) — 读者预期 7 原则
345	- [Lipton: Heuristics for Scientific Writing](https://www.approximatelycorrect.com/2018/01/29/heuristics-technical-scientific-writing-machine-learning-perspective/) — 用词
346	- [Perez: Easy Paper Writing Tips](https://ethanperez.net/easy-paper-writing-tips/) — 微观清晰度
347	
348	**API：**
349	- [Semantic Scholar](https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/) | [CrossRef](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/) | [arXiv](https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/)
350	
351	**会议官方：**
352	- [NeurIPS](https://neurips.cc/) | [ICML](https://icml.cc/) | [ICLR](https://iclr.cc/) | [ACL](https://www.aclweb.org/) | [AAAI](https://aaai.org/) | [EMNLP](https://2025.emnlp.org/)
353

# LaTeX 论文写作全流程

ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。

---

## 1. 工作模式

开始前选择模式：

| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
|------|------|------|
| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |

---

## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论

**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**

### 2.1 一句话贡献

在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。

### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map

为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：

| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |

**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**

### 2.3 章节起草顺序

```
1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
3. Related Work
4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
```

### 2.4 Quality Gates

投稿前必须通过：
- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta

---

## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）

**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**

### 3.1 黄金法则

```
IF 无法程序化获取引用:
    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
    → 明确告知用户
    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
```

### 3.2 五步验证流程

```
1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
```

### 3.3 API 速查

| API | 用途 | 限制 |
|-----|------|------|
| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |

```python
# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
import requests
def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

# Semantic Scholar 搜索
from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
sch = SemanticScholar()
results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
for p in results:
    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
```

### 3.4 引用处理规则

| 情况 | 处理 |
|------|------|
| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

---

## 4. 顶会模板速查

### 4.1 ML/AI 会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |

### 4.2 系统会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |

### 4.3 模板使用原则

```bash
# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/

# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
latexmk -pdf main.tex

# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
```

**禁止事项：**
- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

---

## 5. 写作规范

### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）

花**大致相等**的时间在：
1. Abstract
2. Introduction
3. 图表
4. **其余所有内容加起来**

审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。

### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）

```
1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
2. 为什么这很难且重要
3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
4. 有什么证据
5. 最惊人的数字/结果
```

删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~

### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）

| 原则 | 规则 |
|------|------|
| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |

### 5.4 常见修改

| 问题 | 修复 |
|------|------|
| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |

---

## 6. 投稿工程链

### 6.1 构建

```bash
# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex

# 手动：需要多次编译
pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
```

### 6.2 Lint + 格式化

```bash
# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
chktex main.tex

# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
latexindent -w main.tex
```

### 6.3 图表格式

| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |

```latex
\usepackage{booktabs}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
\midrule
Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
```

**图表规范：**
- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）

### 6.4 投稿打包

```bash
# 清理辅助文件
latexmk -c

# 打包投稿
zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
```

### 6.5 常见失败点

| 问题 | 解决 |
|------|------|
| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |

---

## 7. 会议转投

当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：

### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换

| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
|------|---------|---------|
| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |

### 7.2 转投原则

1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等

---

## 8. 投前清单

### 通用清单

- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
- [ ] 符合页数限制
- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning

### 会议特定

| 会议 | 额外要求 |
|------|---------|
| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |

---

1	\section{Introduction}
2	
3	SwiGLU feed-forward networks~\cite{shazeer2020glu} in modern LLMs exhibit high contextual sparsity: at any given token, a large fraction of FFN neurons contribute negligibly to the output.
4	Exploiting this sparsity can yield up to 2$\times$ inference speedup by pruning 50\% of FFN neurons per token---without modifying the pretrained weights.
5	Yet the gap between potential and practice remains wide.
6	Training-free methods such as TEAL~\cite{liu2025teal} select neurons by activation magnitude alone, degrading perplexity from 6.12 (dense) to 23.31 at 50\% sparsity on LLaMA-3.1-8B~\cite{grattafiori2024llama3}---a 281\% increase.
7	Learned predictors~\cite{liu2023dejavu,gautam2026fastforward} close part of this gap by training small auxiliary networks to anticipate which neurons will be important, but they rely on error compensation modules (output rescaling networks or additive correction layers) that add latency and memory overhead at inference.
8	The question is whether a predictor can be trained so that compensation becomes unnecessary.
9	
10	The answer depends on the training objective.
11	Current learned predictors use binary cross-entropy (BCE) loss: each neuron is independently classified as ``keep'' or ``prune'' against an oracle mask derived from the dense model's activations.
12	The gradient of BCE with respect to neuron $j$'s score is $\partial \mathcal{L}_{\text{BCE}} / \partial s_j = \sigma(s_j) - m_j^*$---a function of neuron $j$ alone, independent of every other neuron in the network.
13	But at inference, no neuron is evaluated in isolation.
14	TEAL's global top-$k$ mechanism~\cite{liu2025teal} ranks all neurons across all layers and retains only those above a model-wide threshold.
15	Whether neuron $j$ survives depends not on its own score but on how that score compares to the scores of all $L \times d_{\text{ff}}$ neurons.
16	This creates a structural mismatch: the training objective decomposes per neuron, while the inference allocation is a global combinatorial decision.
17	BCE can achieve $>$90\% per-neuron classification accuracy against oracle masks yet still produce poor output quality under global allocation, because it optimizes a proxy misaligned with the true objective.
18	
19	KL divergence resolves this mismatch by coupling all neurons through the output distribution.
20	Instead of classifying individual neurons, we minimize $D_{\text{KL}}(p_{\text{dense}} \| p_{\text{sparse}})$ between the dense and sparse model outputs, training the predictor to preserve the full next-token distribution under pruning.
21	The gradient for neuron $j$ in layer $\ell$ factors as:
22	\begin{equation*}
23	\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}}{\partial s_j^{(\ell)}} = \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}}{\partial \mathbf{z}} \cdot \frac{\partial \mathbf{z}}{\partial \mathbf{h}^{(\ell)}} \cdot \frac{\partial \mathbf{h}^{(\ell)}}{\partial \tilde{m}_j^{(\ell)}} \cdot \frac{\partial \tilde{m}_j^{(\ell)}}{\partial s_j^{(\ell)}},
24	\end{equation*}
25	where the Jacobian $\partial \mathbf{z} / \partial \mathbf{h}^{(\ell)}$ propagates through all downstream layers, making each neuron's gradient dependent on every other neuron's mask state.
26	Changing one neuron's mask affects all output logits; KL captures this because it measures distributional divergence over the entire vocabulary.
27	A Gumbel-Sigmoid relaxation~\cite{jang2017gumbel} provides differentiable mask sampling during training, bridging the gap between soft training masks and hard inference decisions.
28	The predictor itself is a lightweight two-layer MLP (Linear $4096 \to 128$, GELU, Linear $128 \to 14336$) with 2.37M parameters per layer and 75.9M total---under 1\% of the base model---and requires no compensation network at inference.
29	
30	Empirically, the structural argument is borne out across sparsity levels, training budgets, and architectures.
31	At 50\% sparsity on LLaMA-3.1-8B, the KL-trained predictor achieves PPL 11.79 under TEAL's global allocation, compared to 23.31 for vanilla TEAL.
32	BCE trained for 2700 steps (2.71$\times$ our compute budget) reaches only 27.97, and its training loss saturates with $\Delta = -0.006$ over the final 2200 steps---confirming that the failure is structural, not computational.
33	The KL advantage scales super-linearly with sparsity: 18\% relative improvement at 30\%, 49\% at 50\%, and 82\% at 70\%.
34	Cross-architecture evaluation on Mistral-7B-v0.3~\cite{jiang2023mistral} yields +63\% relative degradation from dense, compared to +93\% on LLaMA, confirming generalization to SwiGLU models with different attention configurations.
35	We also analyze SPON's~\cite{xu2026spon} static bias correction and find it near-orthogonal to the predictor's effect (cosine similarity 0.196), recovering only 2.4\% of remaining error---the KL predictor already captures most of the recoverable signal.
36	
37	To situate these findings, we propose a two-dimensional taxonomy (Figure~\ref{fig:taxonomy}) that classifies sparsity prediction methods along \emph{correction granularity} (static, per-layer, per-token) and \emph{training signal coupling} (decomposed, intermediate, coupled).
38	Prior methods occupy distinct cells: SPON~\cite{xu2026spon} combines static correction with coupled KL training; ShadowLLM~\cite{akhauri2024shadowllm} uses per-layer prediction with intermediate MSE; FastForward~\cite{gautam2026fastforward} and DejaVu~\cite{liu2023dejavu} achieve per-token granularity but with decomposed BCE objectives.
39	No prior work has combined per-token contextual prediction with a coupled training signal.
40	Our method fills this cell, unifying input-dependent mask generation with an objective that reflects global neuron interactions through the output distribution.
41	
42	Our contributions are:
43	\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
44	\item We show that a KL-trained contextual predictor eliminates the need for error compensation networks in activation sparsity, and provide a formal gradient analysis explaining the structural mismatch between per-neuron BCE training and global top-$k$ inference allocation.
45	\item We propose a 2D taxonomy (correction granularity $\times$ training signal coupling) that unifies existing activation sparsity methods (Figure~\ref{fig:taxonomy}) and identifies the previously unexplored cell our method occupies.
46	\item We identify a phase transition in sparsity regimes---allocation-fixable ($\leq$30\%, where predictor and allocation choices recover downstream performance) vs.\ capacity-limited ($\geq$50\%, where no method recovers reasoning ability)---and confirm via SPON orthogonality analysis that static correction provides diminishing returns once a coupled predictor is present.
47	\end{itemize}

\section{Introduction}

SwiGLU feed-forward networks~\cite{shazeer2020glu} in modern LLMs exhibit high contextual sparsity: at any given token, a large fraction of FFN neurons contribute negligibly to the output.
Exploiting this sparsity can yield up to 2$\times$ inference speedup by pruning 50\% of FFN neurons per token---without modifying the pretrained weights.
Yet the gap between potential and practice remains wide.
Training-free methods such as TEAL~\cite{liu2025teal} select neurons by activation magnitude alone, degrading perplexity from 6.12 (dense) to 23.31 at 50\% sparsity on LLaMA-3.1-8B~\cite{grattafiori2024llama3}---a 281\% increase.
Learned predictors~\cite{liu2023dejavu,gautam2026fastforward} close part of this gap by training small auxiliary networks to anticipate which neurons will be important, but they rely on error compensation modules (output rescaling networks or additive correction layers) that add latency and memory overhead at inference.
The question is whether a predictor can be trained so that compensation becomes unnecessary.

The answer depends on the training objective.
Current learned predictors use binary cross-entropy (BCE) loss: each neuron is independently classified as ``keep'' or ``prune'' against an oracle mask derived from the dense model's activations.
The gradient of BCE with respect to neuron $j$'s score is $\partial \mathcal{L}_{\text{BCE}} / \partial s_j = \sigma(s_j) - m_j^*$---a function of neuron $j$ alone, independent of every other neuron in the network.
But at inference, no neuron is evaluated in isolation.
TEAL's global top-$k$ mechanism~\cite{liu2025teal} ranks all neurons across all layers and retains only those above a model-wide threshold.
Whether neuron $j$ survives depends not on its own score but on how that score compares to the scores of all $L \times d_{\text{ff}}$ neurons.
This creates a structural mismatch: the training objective decomposes per neuron, while the inference allocation is a global combinatorial decision.
BCE can achieve $>$90\% per-neuron classification accuracy against oracle masks yet still produce poor output quality under global allocation, because it optimizes a proxy misaligned with the true objective.

KL divergence resolves this mismatch by coupling all neurons through the output distribution.
Instead of classifying individual neurons, we minimize $D_{\text{KL}}(p_{\text{dense}} \| p_{\text{sparse}})$ between the dense and sparse model outputs, training the predictor to preserve the full next-token distribution under pruning.
The gradient for neuron $j$ in layer $\ell$ factors as:
\begin{equation*}
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}}{\partial s_j^{(\ell)}} = \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}}{\partial \mathbf{z}} \cdot \frac{\partial \mathbf{z}}{\partial \mathbf{h}^{(\ell)}} \cdot \frac{\partial \mathbf{h}^{(\ell)}}{\partial \tilde{m}_j^{(\ell)}} \cdot \frac{\partial \tilde{m}_j^{(\ell)}}{\partial s_j^{(\ell)}},
\end{equation*}
where the Jacobian $\partial \mathbf{z} / \partial \mathbf{h}^{(\ell)}$ propagates through all downstream layers, making each neuron's gradient dependent on every other neuron's mask state.
Changing one neuron's mask affects all output logits; KL captures this because it measures distributional divergence over the entire vocabulary.
A Gumbel-Sigmoid relaxation~\cite{jang2017gumbel} provides differentiable mask sampling during training, bridging the gap between soft training masks and hard inference decisions.
The predictor itself is a lightweight two-layer MLP (Linear $4096 \to 128$, GELU, Linear $128 \to 14336$) with 2.37M parameters per layer and 75.9M total---under 1\% of the base model---and requires no compensation network at inference.

Empirically, the structural argument is borne out across sparsity levels, training budgets, and architectures.
At 50\% sparsity on LLaMA-3.1-8B, the KL-trained predictor achieves PPL 11.79 under TEAL's global allocation, compared to 23.31 for vanilla TEAL.
BCE trained for 2700 steps (2.71$\times$ our compute budget) reaches only 27.97, and its training loss saturates with $\Delta = -0.006$ over the final 2200 steps---confirming that the failure is structural, not computational.
The KL advantage scales super-linearly with sparsity: 18\% relative improvement at 30\%, 49\% at 50\%, and 82\% at 70\%.
Cross-architecture evaluation on Mistral-7B-v0.3~\cite{jiang2023mistral} yields +63\% relative degradation from dense, compared to +93\% on LLaMA, confirming generalization to SwiGLU models with different attention configurations.
We also analyze SPON's~\cite{xu2026spon} static bias correction and find it near-orthogonal to the predictor's effect (cosine similarity 0.196), recovering only 2.4\% of remaining error---the KL predictor already captures most of the recoverable signal.

To situate these findings, we propose a two-dimensional taxonomy (Figure~\ref{fig:taxonomy}) that classifies sparsity prediction methods along \emph{correction granularity} (static, per-layer, per-token) and \emph{training signal coupling} (decomposed, intermediate, coupled).
Prior methods occupy distinct cells: SPON~\cite{xu2026spon} combines static correction with coupled KL training; ShadowLLM~\cite{akhauri2024shadowllm} uses per-layer prediction with intermediate MSE; FastForward~\cite{gautam2026fastforward} and DejaVu~\cite{liu2023dejavu} achieve per-token granularity but with decomposed BCE objectives.
No prior work has combined per-token contextual prediction with a coupled training signal.
Our method fills this cell, unifying input-dependent mask generation with an objective that reflects global neuron interactions through the output distribution.

Our contributions are:
\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
\item We show that a KL-trained contextual predictor eliminates the need for error compensation networks in activation sparsity, and provide a formal gradient analysis explaining the structural mismatch between per-neuron BCE training and global top-$k$ inference allocation.
\item We propose a 2D taxonomy (correction granularity $\times$ training signal coupling) that unifies existing activation sparsity methods (Figure~\ref{fig:taxonomy}) and identifies the previously unexplored cell our method occupies.
\item We identify a phase transition in sparsity regimes---allocation-fixable ($\leq$30\%, where predictor and allocation choices recover downstream performance) vs.\ capacity-limited ($\geq$50\%, where no method recovers reasoning ability)---and confirm via SPON orthogonality analysis that static correction provides diminishing returns once a coupled predictor is present.
\end{itemize}

Activation sparsity can accelerate SwiGLU-based LLMs by pruning FFN neurons at inference, but existing learned predictors trained with binary cross-entropy (BCE) require error compensation networks due to a structural mismatch: BCE decomposes per neuron while inference uses global top-$k$ allocation across all layers.
We train lightweight predictors (2.37M parameters per layer, 75.9M total, $<$1\% of the base model) with KL divergence, which couples all neurons through the output distribution via Gumbel-Sigmoid relaxation, eliminating the need for compensation.
On LLaMA-3.1-8B (WikiText-2), our KL-trained predictor achieves perplexity 11.79 at 50\% sparsity, compared to 23.31 for vanilla TEAL and 27.97 for BCE trained at 2.71$\times$ the compute budget---whose loss saturates, confirming a structural rather than computational failure.
The KL advantage scales super-linearly with sparsity: 18\% relative improvement at 30\%, 49\% at 50\%, and 82\% at 70\%.
Cross-architecture evaluation on Mistral-7B-v0.3 yields +63\% degradation versus +93\% for TEAL.
SPON's static bias correction proves near-orthogonal to the predictor (cosine similarity 0.196), recovering only 2.4\% of residual error.
We propose a two-dimensional taxonomy over correction granularity $\times$ training signal coupling that unifies prior methods and identify a phase transition between allocation-fixable and capacity-limited sparsity regimes.
